title: Learning Permutation Distributions via Reflected Diffusion on Ranks
claim: Corrupt discrete objects by evolving a continuous latent whose sorted order induces the discrete state, and reverse it by alternating discrete denoising with latent updates.
layout: 2 stacked bands, continuous above discrete, forward left, reverse right, dotted links
description: The figure has two stacked rounded panels. The top panel, labeled Continuous space, holds two noisy-trajectory plots: Forward Process (t from 0 to 1) and Reverse Process (t from 1 to 0). Each plot has four colored random-walk curves, which are the soft ranks, and two vertical shaded bars marking time points. The bottom panel, labeled Discrete space, shows columns of four card-suit icons (club, heart, spade, diamond). They are shuffled from X0 through intermediate states to X1 by blue arrows. On the right, the reverse side goes from Xt through a denoiser p_theta to a predicted X0-hat. Dotted arrows link the discrete columns to points on the continuous curves. These dotted arrows stand for inducing an ordering and for lifting to soft ranks. Z_t, Z_s and Z0-hat = [1/3, 0, 1, 2/3] sit above the reverse columns. A legend at the bottom left defines the symbols and arrow types.
caption: Soft-Rank Diffusion. We define the forward diffusion by relaxing each item’s rank to a continuous soft-rank variable and evolving these soft ranks in a reflected diffusion process (Lou & Ermon, 2023). At each time t, the soft ranks induce a discrete ordering by simple sorting, thereby yielding a forward process in permutation space. For reverse sampling, we couple a discrete denoiser in permutation space (predicting a clean permutation from Xt) with an auxiliary continuous update: we lift the predicted permutation to a grid-aligned soft-rank vector ˆZ0, sample an intermediate latent Zs for s < t from a conditional reverse kernel p(Zs | Zt, ˆZ0, Z1), and map back to permutation space by sorting Zs, thus stepping backward in time.
abstract: The finite symmetric group S_n provides a natural domain for permutations, yet learning probability distributions on S_n is challenging due to its factorially growing size and discrete, non-Euclidean structure. Recent permutation diffusion methods define forward noising via shuffle-based random walks (e.g., riffle shuffles) and learn reverse transitions with Plackett-Luce (PL) variants, but the resulting trajectories can be abrupt and increasingly hard to denoise as n grows. We propose Soft-Rank Diffusion, a discrete diffusion framework that replaces shuffle-based corruption with a structured soft-rank forward process: we lift permutations to a continuous latent representation of order by relaxing discrete ranks into soft ranks, yielding smoother and more tractable trajectories. For the reverse process, we introduce contextualized generalized Plackett-Luce (cGPL) denoisers that generalize prior PL-style parameterizations and improve expressivity for sequential decision structures. Experiments on sorting and combinatorial optimization benchmarks show that Soft-Rank Diffusion consistently outperforms prior diffusion baselines, with particularly strong gains in long-sequence and intrinsically sequential settings.
